properties.name: A fact may carry its date as a property, and search_design reads it back with its age
properties.rationale: Measured first: 112 of 205 TemporalFacts carried the property, 76 the edge, ZERO both. A clean split with no node caught between the two conventions is what a missing word looks like, not what carelessness looks like — the edge demands a DesignEpoch and a writer holding a date has nothing to point it at. Anthony chose (a) over migrating the 112 into invented epochs, and over making the edge polymorphic. The scope then grew on evidence: there was no reader to fall back, so one was built.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Implements `dec:how-should-a-temporal-fact-carry-its-date-when-there-is-no-epoch`, option (a), settled on Anthony's word 2026-08-16.

WHAT CHANGED. `TemporalFact` declares `valid_from` and `valid_to` as date-string properties (`schema/temporal.yaml`). A new `reflow2-core::dates` module converts `YYYY-MM-DD` to a day number and subtracts. `SearchHit` gains a flattened `ClaimAge`, so `search_design` returns `as_of`, `age_days` and `expired` for any node carrying a date, and returns nothing extra for any node that does not.

⭐ THE SCOPE GREW ON EVIDENCE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The decision said "declare the properties, and have readers prefer the edge and fall back to the property". Checking what actually reads `VALID_FROM` found ONE reader — `readiness.rs:653` — which filters to `basis: forecast`, AND THERE ARE ZERO FORECAST FACTS IN THE DESIGN. All 189 dated facts are `measured`. So the 76 edge-bearing facts were just as unread in practice as the 112 property-bearing ones, and there was no reader to teach. Declaring the property alone would have changed the schema and left the corpus exactly as inert as before — which `dec:edge-orthogonality` forbids: a vocabulary distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it. So the reader was built, and the property ships with it.

⭐ THE READER WAS ALREADY DESIGNED AND UNBUILT. `cap:claims-carry-their-age` part 3 reads: "where-am-i and search_design mark how old a node's factual half is, so a six-week-old observation is not narrated as current." A date string is exactly what that needs; an epoch reference is not, because an epoch carries a `sequence` for ordering and not a calendar position. This lands that part.

THE EXTRACTION HINT IS CORRECTED, and it was the cause rather than a detail. It read "a satisfaction fact whose VALID_FROM is a later epoch; a dropped requirement = a fact with VALID_TO set" — describing as fields two things that were edges. That is what taught 112 writers to invent the properties. It now states plainly that there are two ways to say when, that they are not interchangeable, and which to prefer.

DELIBERATE SHAPE, each chosen against a cheaper alternative:
- NO `chrono`. The core is dependency-light and the requirement is one subtraction; the civil-date conversion is a known closed form in fifteen lines.
- `today` IS A PARAMETER on everything that decides. Only `today_utc()` reads the clock, at the edge. A function that reads the clock cannot be tested, only observed — and a module about staleness must not have tests that pass today and fail in a fortnight.
- THE CLOCK IS READ ONCE PER RESULT LIST, not once per hit, so two hits can never disagree about what day it is.
- `as_of` AND `age_days` ARE SEPARATE FIELDS so that "dated, but the date will not parse" is sayable. Collapsing them would make an unreadable date indistinguishable from no date.
- AN UNREADABLE `valid_to` NEVER EXPIRES A CLAIM. Guessing would silently retire live facts.
- A FUTURE DATE REPORTS A NEGATIVE AGE rather than clamping to zero, because clamping renders a forecast or a typo as "current" — the exact misreading the capability exists to prevent.

VERIFIED. 15 cases in `a_claim_carries_its_age.rs`, all passing, including the Gregorian century exceptions (1900 not a leap year, 2000 one) that a naive `% 4` or `% 100` gets wrong. FOUR MUTATIONS, each killed by the right case: dropping the century exception fails the leap and anchor cases; clamping a future date fails the negative-age case; expiring on the last valid day fails the boundary case; treating an unreadable end date as expired fails the counterweight. END-TO-END on the real store through a restarted server: a fact dated today returned `age_days: 0`, one dated 2026-08-07 returned `age_days: 9`, and an undated fact returned no age fields at all — all three in one reply.

NO SCHEMA STAMP MOVEMENT: properties are not counted by the version stamp, only node and edge types are, so no upgrade document is owed.

NOT DONE, and named rather than left to be discovered: the 112 existing facts are not migrated or normalised — they are simply read now. Nothing writes `valid_from` automatically; it remains something an author states. And `where-am-i`, the other half of `cap:claims-carry-their-age` part 3, still does not mark age.
